items.title: Rendang is not supposed to be crispy, but who owns it?
items.summary: LETTERS: A chef and a lawyer on lost recipes, and how to keep them alive. One of us cooks. Rendang is slow.

items.title: RM1.18mil rewards paid to 652 civil servants for reporting bribery
items.summary: Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said 529 individuals were recommended to receive cash rewards and certificates of appreciation, while another 123 received certificates for their outstanding commitment to curbing corruption. He said the rewards and recognition had helped strengthen a culture of integrity within the public service. Abd Halim had earlier chaired the 15th Recognition Assessment Panel Meeting for Civil Servants Reporting Bribery Offers or Receipt of Bribes at the MACC headquarters in Putrajaya.

items.title: Rapid KL deploys alternative trains after Putrajaya Line brake system malfunction at Jalan Ipoh Station
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — A brake system malfunction on a train at Jalan Ipoh Station caused a disruption on the Putrajaya Line today, Rapid KL said. Rapid KL said it activated alternative train services to maintain passenger movement along affected stretches of the line. Rapid KL listed the following alternative train arrangements: Trains from Kwasa Damansara Station turning back at Jalan Ipoh Station — five‑minute intervals Trains from Hospital Kuala Lumpur Station turning back at Putrajaya Sentral Station — six‑minute intervals Shuttle service between Kentonmen Station and Hospital Kuala Lumpur Station — seven‑minute intervals Rapid KL said updates would be issued through its official social media channels and the MyRapid PULSE application.

items.title: Sarawak radio presenter dies at age 47 after collapsing at Kuching RTM office
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 23 — A radio presenter for RED FM at Radio Televisyen Malaysia (RTM) Sarawak, Azrani Azmi, 47, died after being found unconscious at his office at RTM Sarawak last night. His younger sister, NurFarrah Hanna Azmi, said colleagues found him at about 8.40pm and rushed him to Sarawak General Hospital. — Bernama

items.title: Penang Hospital carries out third kidney retrieval this year
items.summary: https://www.facebook.com/share/1Ek97Srz9d/?mibextid=wwXIfr GEORGE TOWN: Penang Hospital has successfully retrieved both kidneys from a deceased donor, marking its third such procedure this year. The state Health Department and Penang Hospital said the donor was a woman who served as her family's breadwinner and died after suffering a ruptured intracranial aneurysm. The department said the hospital's Transport Unit, Organ Procurement Unit and National Transplant Centre also contributed to the kidney retrieval.

items.title: South Korea plans to cut Middle East crude oil imports to 50pct by 2035
items.summary: SEOUL: South Korea aims to reduce its reliance on crude oil from the Middle East to 50 per cent by 2035, as Asia's fourth-biggest economy seeks to diversify energy supplies following the disruption caused by the Iran war, the Industry Ministry said on Wednesday. South Korea relies heavily on oil imports and sourced 70 per cent of its supplies from the Middle East in 2025, most of it delivered through the Strait of Hormuz, according to the ministry. South Korea also aims to secure additional supplies of condensate, an ultra-light oil mainly used to produce naphtha, the ministry said.

items.title: Australian competition regulator blocks IAG's RAC Insurance takeover
items.summary: SYDNEY: Australia's competition regulator on Wednesday blocked Insurance Australia Group's planned takeover of RAC Insurance, finding it would likely weaken competition in key insurance markets in Western Australia. Here are some more details: * The regulator said the acquisition could reduce competition in the supply of motor vehicle insurance and home and contents insurance in Western Australia. * "The acquisition would combine two large insurers, resulting in a substantial increase in IAG's market share and a significant increase in market concentration," ACCC Chair Gina Cass-Gottlieb said.

items.title: Haze worsens: Two Sarawak areas hit ‘very unhealthy’ API levels, Kanowit at 244, Lubok Antu at 205
items.summary: Lubok Antu recorded an API reading of 205. All other areas, except Bario, recorded API readings in the ‘Unhealthy’ category. Mukah recorded an API of 162, while Samalaju and Miri both registered API readings of 158.

items.title: US to fund US$7bil of Argentina mineral, energy projects
items.summary: NEW YORK: The US Export-Import Bank plans to fund up to US$7 billion worth of critical minerals and energy projects in Argentina, according to a document seen by Reuters, as part of a push to deepen economic cooperation between Washington and Buenos Aires. Argentina's Congress has yet to ratify the bilateral deal. Argentina has large deposits of lithium, shale oil and other commodities.

items.title: YTL AI Labs, Nvidia launch 1.35mil persona Malaysian AI dataset
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: YTL AI Labs has teamed up with Nvidia to launch an open dataset containing 1.35 million synthetic Malaysian personas, in a move aimed at giving developers and enterprises a locally grounded foundation for building and testing artificial intelligence (AI) systems. In a statement, YTL AI Labs said the dataset is designed to capture Malaysia's demographic, linguistic, cultural and regional diversity, allowing AI developers to build systems that better reflect the population they are intended to serve. The launch also strengthens YTL Group's push to build a broader sovereign AI ecosystem in Malaysia, spanning computing infrastructure, locally developed AI models and data designed around Malaysian users.

items.title: China Eastern upgrades app as Malaysia-China travel demand grows
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: China Eastern Airlines has upgraded its international mobile app, potentially giving travellers a more streamlined digital experience when booking and managing flights to China and other international destinations. The airline said version 2.0 of its international app is now available on the App Store and Google Play, with upgrades focused on flight booking, seat selection, itinerary management and access to real-time flight information. For Malaysian travellers, the enhanced platform comes as China remains an important destination for tourism and business travel, with China Eastern operating international services linking Malaysia with China and its wider network.

items.title: Raja of Perlis grants audience to Indonesian ambassador to Malaysia
items.summary: ARAU: The Raja of Perlis, Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin Jamalullail, granted an audience to the Ambassador of the Republic of Indonesia to Malaysia, Raden Datuk Mohammad Iman Hascarya, at the Blue Audience Hall, Istana Arau, here yesterday. Istana Arau, in a statement today, said the meeting underscored the longstanding relationship between Malaysia, including Perlis, and Indonesia. According to Istana Arau, ties between Perlis and Indonesia have been strengthened through cooperation in education, particularly with the establishment of Universiti Muhammadiyah Malaysia (UMAM) in the state.

items.title: Tribunal orders former director of a Sabah hospital to apologise, pay RM10,000 over sexual harassment complaint
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 23 — A former Sabah hospital director has been ordered by the Tribunal for Anti-Sexual Harassment (TAGS) to pay RM10,000 in compensation to a woman who lodged a police report alleging sexual harassment against him. His counsel Joan Goh (pic) said TAGS also ordered her client to apologise to the woman and pay the compensation via bank transfer within 30 days of the award dated Sept 18. Goh said her client would challenge the Tribunal’s decision in the High Court through judicial review and seek a stay of the award pending determination of the challenge.

items.title: Geopolitics, rates, AI demand to shape APAC markets in 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Financial markets in 2026, including Malaysia, are being shaped by a mix of geopolitical risks, energy price volatility, interest rate expectations and uneven economic growth, creating divergent opportunities across currencies, commodities and equity indices, according to JustMarkets. The global backdrop remains mixed, with International Monetary Fund (IMF) estimates putting world gross domestic product (GDP) growth at 3.0 per cent this year. In the Asia-Pacific (APAC) region, monetary policy, currency movements, technology demand and equity markets are among the key factors influencing trading activity.

items.title: Hajiji: Sabah can play bigger role in Malaysia-China ties
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Sept 23 — Sabah is in a strategic position to become an important bridge in further strengthening cooperation between Malaysia and China, said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor. He said Sabah’s ties with China form an important part of the broader Malaysia-China cooperation, with relations between the two sides having been established for a long time through maritime trade routes. China is one of Sabah’s most important trading partners, with cooperation encompassing commodities, agriculture, fisheries, manufactured products, tourism, and services.

items.title: Anwar to meet 21 Chinese business leaders in Shanghai and Hangzhou as Malaysia courts fresh investment
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 23 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to hold a roundtable business engagement and deliver a keynote address at the WorldSkills Conference 2026 here today. He will then attend the opening ceremony of the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 competition, to be officiated by Chinese Premier Li Qiang at the National Exhibition and Convention Centre. Held from Sept 22 to 27, WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 is a major international platform showcasing excellence in technical and vocational skills.

items.title: Thai imam’s wife finds paint splashed on car after prayers in Tumpat, Kelantan police on the case
items.summary: Tumpat police chief ACP Mohd Khairi Shafie said the 30-year-old imam had parked the white Honda City near the jetty at 7.10pm before heading to Masjid Pulau Beluru for Isyak prayers. “The complainant, however, denied the allegation,” he said. Anyone with information is urged to contact the Tumpat District Police Headquarters operations room at 09-7252482 or the nearest police station.

items.title: The Melaka assembly is dissolved. What's next?
items.summary: MELAKA: Following the dissolution of the Melaka state assembly, the state administration enters a transition phase governed by constitutional protocols and election regulations. The 60-day constitutional window Under the Melaka State Constitution, a state election must be conducted within 60 days from the date of the assembly's dissolution. Notification: The Speaker of the State Legislative Assembly will formally notify the Election Commission (EC) of the dissolution.

items.title: #NSTViral: Hundreds of dead fish found floating at Ampang Hilir lake after heavy rain
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Hundreds of dead fish were spotted floating at Taman Tasik Ampang Hilir following several days of heavy rain in the city, prompting concern among park-goers and social media users. The fish deaths also raised concerns over a strong stench and possible water contamination at the public recreational area. "Floating fish, dead fish.

items.title: Landslide forces Cheras apartment residents out of their homes, underground water leak suspected
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — Residents of an apartment block in Bandar Damai Perdana, Cheras, were ordered to evacuate their homes last night following a landslide near the building, believed to have been caused by an underground water leak. Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant operations director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the on-site operations commander ordered residents near Block A of the apartment complex to immediately evacuate their homes as a precautionary measure. He said the department received an emergency call regarding the incident at 9:03pm, and a team of five personnel with a fire engine from Bandar Tun Hussein Onn Fire and Rescue Station was deployed to the scene.

items.title: Negri Sembilan, people must not become victims of power struggle — Amanah Youth
items.summary: SEREMBAN: Negri Sembilan Parti Amanah Negara (Amanah) Youth has urged all parties not to exploit the state's royal institution crisis to create unrest, division or instability. Its Communications director Zainal Lutfi Zainal Fitry said all actions by any party must be guided by the Negri Sembilan Constitution 1959, Federal Constitution, rule of law and lawful legal processes. "Negri Sembilan Amanah Youth takes note of the latest developments concerning the cancellation of the appointment of members of the State Executive Council (Exco) by Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.

items.title: Turkiye's Erdogan urges world to 'immediately' start rebuilding Gaza
items.summary: UNITED NATIONS: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said on Tuesday that the world must immediately start the reconstruction of the devastated Gaza Strip. "We must begin the reconstruction of Gaza immediately," he told the United Nations General Assembly, urging world leaders to "exert greater pressure on Israel". Since Hamas fighters launched their Oct 7, 2023, attack on Israel, triggering a massive response, the tiny Palestinian territory has been devastated by countless Israeli airstrikes, which by October 2025 had left 84 per cent of all structures damaged or destroyed, UN figures show.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan exco overstepped its powers by suspending two top officials, says AGC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 23 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) has stated that the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council has no legal authority to suspend the duties of the state secretary (SUK) and state legal adviser. “On the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar’s Sept 22, 2026 media statement suspending the SUK and state legal adviser with immediate effect, this department is of the view that the Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council has no legal authority to do so,” the AGC said. Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim today announced the immediate suspension of the duties of SUK Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and state legal adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal.

items.title: Melaka state election: Eight seats to watch
items.summary: PENGKALAN BATU (N15) - 2021 majority: 131 votes - Winning party: BN (Umno) - Significance: One of the narrowest majorities in the state. DUYONG (N21) - 2021 Majority: 200 votes - Winning party: BN (Umno) - Significance: Previously held by DAP before flipping to Umno in 2021. TANJUNG BIDARA (N02) 2021 majority: 364 votes Winning party: BN (Umno) Significance: A high-profile seat contested in 2021 by Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh.

items.title: Strengthening community ties through outreach in Desa Mentari
items.summary: PETALING JAYA: When around 2,000 members of the Desa Mentari community gathered at the Petaling Jaya City Council Multipurpose Hall to celebrate Malaysia Day, the occasion marked more than the close of Sunway Group's month-long #SunwayforGood Food Programme. It also strengthened an ongoing relationship between Sunway and the community through the Sunway Desa Mentari Community Development Programme. At the heart of the programme was Burger Rumah Sahabat, a business that emerged from Sunway's collaboration with Selangor Youth Community (SAY).

items.title: Laying the building blocks for RM10bil market cap
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Lim Seong Hai Capital Bhd (LSH) is laying the building blocks that would take the group to a market value of RM10 billion within the next five years, as the group prepares to be transferred to the Main Market of Bursa Malaysia. And Lim claims that he knows how to bring LSH to a market cap of RM10 billion within the next five years. 5 years.

items.title: 13 areas in Sarawak record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Thirteen areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy air quality readings as of 8am today. Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System data showed that Sri Aman recorded the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading in the country at 181. Eight areas recorded good air quality, with Banting recording the highest API reading in the category at 47.

items.title: Melaka election: PH raring to go as talks continue
items.summary: Kota Melaka member of parliament Khoo Poay Tiong said the dissolution came as no surprise, given earlier indications by caretaker chief minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh that the 28-seat assembly would be dissolved this month. PH is ready to face the election. Our party members are ready," he said.

items.title: Trump says US-Iran talks have 'momentum', could lead to deal
items.summary: WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Tuesday that talks with Iran had gained momentum and could lead to a deal, but warned that the United States could take additional military action against Iranian nuclear facilities if necessary, Anadolu Ajansi reported. He said US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner had held a "productive meeting" with mediators involved in efforts to engage Iran. That's what we are hearing from everybody," said Trump.

items.title: Anwar to meet industry leaders, deliver keynote address and travel to Hangzhou
items.summary: SHANGHAI: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to hold a roundtable business engagement and deliver a keynote address at the WorldSkills Conference 2026 here today. He will then attend the opening ceremony of the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 competition, to be officiated by Chinese Premier Li Qiang at the National Exhibition and Convention Centre (NECC). In the 48th WorldSkills Competition, Malaysia is represented by 22 participants competing in 21 skill categories under the "Road to Gold" agenda, aimed at securing the country's first gold medal at the prestigious global competition.

items.title: Colombia president orders troops to violence-hit Caribbean city
items.summary: BOGOTA: Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella on Tuesday sent troops into the Caribbean city of Santa Marta after gunmen attacked shops and burnt vehicles following the killing of one of their leaders. Videos shared online showed members of the self-styled Conquering Self Defence Forces of the Sierra Nevada (ACSN) riding through the city on motorbikes, firing on businesses that remained open despite the group announcing a 48-hour curfew. "I have ordered...that Santa Marta be militarised," De la Espriella later announced in a video statement.

items.title: First Iran flights cancelled as US sanctions set to come into force
items.summary: The Tasnim news agency cited a civil aviation spokesman as saying that "Baghdad and Muscat airports will no longer accept Iranian flights." According to Tasnim, Iran's aviation authorities are in talks to reroute Baghdad flights to Najaf, a major destination for Iranian pilgrims. Earlier this month, the US blacklisted the Iranian aviation sector and threatened sanctions against any foreign organisation working with Iran's airlines.

items.title: Britain will stand firm over Falklands, UK PM Burnham tells Trump
items.summary: UNITED NATIONS: Prime Minister Andy Burnham set out Britain's position on the Falkland Islands during a meeting with US President Donald Trump on Tuesday, saying he would stand firm in the face of any threats. In August, Trump said he was reviewing the United States' neutral position on the remote archipelago in the South Atlantic. Days later, Argentine President Javier Milei said he would sanction oil companies drilling in the islands.

items.title: Trump renames AI 'super intelligence' as leaders jostle over dangers
items.summary: UNITED NATIONS: US President Donald Trump on Tuesday announced that the US government would rename artificial intelligence "super intelligence" in official communications, as world leaders jostled over how to address the dangers of the fast-advancing technology. AI has become a major topic at the UN General Assembly after incidents of the technology falling out of the control of humans and warnings by company insiders drew global alarm and calls for better government supervision of the industry. French President Emmanuel Macron proposed building AI technology independent from the great powers.

items.title: Trump hails Burnham as 'natural business person' after first meeting
items.summary: UNITED NATIONS: US President Donald Trump hailed Andy Burnham on Tuesday as a "natural business person" at what the new British leader's team described as a smooth first face-to-face meeting. After days of preparation for the Trump meeting, Burnham emerged relatively unscathed, with the US leader only taking issue with what he called a "terrible deal" to cede sovereignty of the Chagos Islands, home to a US-British air base. Otherwise, Trump praised Burnham, saying Britain's seventh prime minister in a decade was someone with whom he could do business and a patriot who had put Britain on the up after replacing the former prime minister, Keir Starmer, in July.

items.title: Melaka state election: How the numbers stack up
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: With the dissolution of the Melaka state legislative assembly dissolved, the state will enter a crucial 60-day election window to elect a new state administration. THE ASSEMBLY AT A GLANCE: Total state seats: 28 Simple majority needed: 15 seats Two-thirds majority needed: 19 seats Registered voters: 495,000 STATUS AT DISSOLUTION VS 2021 ELECTION OUTCOME: - In the last state election held in November 2021, Barisan Nasional (BN) secured a comfortable two-thirds victory by winning 21 out of 28 seats. Pakatan Harapan (PH) won 5 seats, while Perikatan Nasional (PN) captured 2 seats.

items.title: Najib’s house arrest explained: 10 questions about pardons, prison powers and what happens next
items.summary: That distinction has come into focus after former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak was granted a conditional pardon on September 18 allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International jail sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of a RM50 million fine and other conditions. What were the terms of Najib’s September 18 conditional pardon? Najib was granted a conditional pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International jail sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and compliance with other conditions.

items.title: ‘Sometimes I make only RM5’: Traders struggle as Rantau Panjang’s once-bustling bazaar falls quiet
items.summary: PASIR MAS, Sept 23 — There are days when dry food seller Sapinah Abdul Rahman, 66, earns only RM5 to RM10 in profit from her business at Bazar Siti Fatimah in Rantau Panjang. However, its economic hub has now become increasingly quiet, including Bazar Siti Fatimah. When people come, traders like us will also have opportunities to earn a living,” she said.

items.title: Melaka election ahead: Key players, shifting alliances and the possible implications for Putrajaya
items.summary: Melaka, traditionally a Barisan Nasional (BN) stronghold, fell to Pakatan Harapan (PH) for the first time in 2018 before BN wrested the state back with a two-thirds majority in the 2021 state election. BN won 21 seats in the 28-seat state assembly in 2021, while PH secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two. Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh announced yesterday that the state assembly would be dissolved today after receiving the consent of Melaka Governor Tun Mohd Ali Rustam, paving the way for the state’s 16th election.

items.title: 'Looksmaxxing' influencer Clavicular charged with rape in Massachusetts
items.summary: His spokesperson Mitchell Jackson said the accuser had previously filed a lawsuit against Peters. According to court documents, Peters' accuser went to the police in Chatham to report him on June 4. The girl told police she became increasingly intoxicated.

items.title: Trump threatens to annihilate Iran as diplomats push for deal at UN
items.summary: UNITED NATIONS: US President Donald Trump warned on Tuesday that he could annihilate Iran if there is no deal to end the war, but also suggested an agreement could come soon amid a diplomatic push at the United Nations. Trump said that envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner "had a very productive meeting today with mediators of Iran." You never know," Trump said as he met the leaders.

items.title: Israel denounces 'grotesque absurdity' of Macron UN remarks on West Bank
items.summary: JERUSALEM: Israel shot back angrily Tuesday at French President Emmanuel Macron, who criticised Israeli actions in the West Bank by saying Hamas was not active in the territory that is home to the Palestinian Authority. They have murdered countless Israeli civilians in Judea and Samaria," it said, using the Biblical name for the West Bank, which Israel seized in 1967. Extremist Israeli settlers frequently attack and steal from West Bank Palestinians.

items.title: Selangor Malay Reserve Land up 1,084.55 hectares since 2018, says Amirudin
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 22 — The total area of Malay Reserve Land in Selangor has increased by 1,084.55 hectares (2,680 acres) since 2018, said Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. In a statement today, Amirudin said the overall area under the state government’s administration had increased from 162,161.98 hectares (400,711 acres) to 163,246.54 hectares (403,391 acres). “Since 2018, the total area of Malay Reserve Land in Selangor under this administration has increased by 1,084.55 hectares (2,680 acres) compared to the previous government,” he said, in response to questions raised regarding the status of Malay Reserve Land in Sabak Bernam.

items.title: Just 40m long, new Mont Kiara road opens shortcut to Solaris and Segambut
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — A new road measuring just 40 metres has opened in Mont Kiara, creating a direct connection between Jalan Duta Kiara and Jalan Kiara 3 and giving motorists an alternative route towards Solaris Dutamas, Segambut and surrounding areas. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said Jalan Duta Kiara had previously ended in a dead end, forcing motorists travelling between Bukit Pelangi and Solaris to take a longer route despite the two areas being close to one another. Yeoh said the project followed discussions involving the developer, the Mont Kiara Residents’ Association and other local stakeholders over traffic and connectivity concerns in the area.

items.title: KPWKM seeks higher Budget 2027 allowances for disabled workers and PDK staff, says Nancy
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Sept 22 — The Women, Family and Community Development Ministry (KPWKM) has proposed higher allowances for disabled workers and staff at Community Rehabilitation Centres (PDK) under Budget 2027, the minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said. She said the ministry was committed to ensuring that persons with disabilities (PwD) and those involved in caregiving received appropriate support, particularly to improve their quality of life. Nancy said ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027, her ministry also hoped its proposal to strengthen the care economy would be approved.

items.title: MCMC ready to license e-commerce platforms once ministries set conditions, says deputy minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Communications Ministry is waiting for the terms and conditions from the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) and the Finance Ministry (MoF) before licensing e-commerce platforms. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has the power under the existing legal framework to license the platforms, but the specific conditions must be decided by the relevant ministries. MCMC, or the Ministry of Communications, is involved because under the Malaysian legal framework, we have the power to actually license e-commerce platforms.

items.title: Magnitude 4.4 earthquake detected off Batu Pahat, tremors felt onshore
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Sept 22 — A magnitude 4.4 earthquake was detected off the coast of Batu Pahat at 4.55pm today. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the earthquake struck at a depth of 10 kilometres, with its epicentre at 1.7 degrees north and 102.7 degrees east, about 27 kilometres southwest of Batu Pahat. Tremors were felt in Batu Pahat and surrounding areas, MetMalaysia said, adding that it would continue to monitor the situation.

items.title: Sarawak’s next legislative assembly sitting will be the last of current term, says state Speaker
items.summary: KUCHING, Sept 22 — The coming Sarawak Legislative Assembly (DUN) will be the last one for this term, said Speaker Tan Sri Datuk Amar Mohamad Asfia Awang Nassar. However, he said the dates of the coming DUN sitting have not been announced yet. So, I will call a press conference before the DUN,” said Asfia.

items.title: Anwar arrives in Shanghai for three-day working visit
items.summary: SHANGHAI, Sept 22 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived here on Tuesday for a three-day working visit to Shanghai and Hangzhou, China, aimed at strengthening Malaysia-China ties, boosting trade and expanding cooperation in emerging technologies. Also present were Shanghai Vice-Mayor of Shanghai Wang Huajie, China’s Ambassador to Malaysia Ouyang Yujing, and Su Lin, a member of the Party Leadership Group of the Shanghai Municipal Foreign Affairs Office. Anwar, who is also finance minister, is accompanied by Minister of Investment, Trade and Industry, Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani, and Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.

items.title: Melaka to keep running as usual as state assembly heads for dissolution
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 22 — Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh has given assurance that the Melaka state government’s affairs will continue to run as usual even though the Melaka State Legislative Assembly (DUN) is dissolved effective tomorrow. He said the state administration, public service delivery, public welfare affairs, security and the government’s daily services will continue to operate as usual. “Following this dissolution, the state government will carry out its responsibilities in the capacity of a caretaker government until a new state government is formed after the election process.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan govt suspends state secretary, legal adviser amid royal row
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — The Negeri Sembilan government today suspended the state secretary and state legal adviser with immediate effect amid the ongoing dispute involving the state’s royal institution. The two officials are State Secretary Datuk Mohd Zafir Ibrahim and State Legal Adviser Datuk Muzalmah Mustapha Kamal. In a statement, Ismail said State Financial Officer Datuk Masri Razali would assume the duties of the state secretary until a new state secretary is appointed by the Chief Secretary to the Government.

items.title: Tasik Bera enforcement: Five arrested, investigation papers to be referred to DPP
items.summary: Acting Pahang police chief Datuk Azry Akmar Ayob said the reports were lodged by members of the Orang Asli community and enforcement personnel. Azry Akmar said the investigation papers on five individuals arrested on Sept 15 for allegedly obstructing enforcement officers during the operation would be referred to the Deputy Public Prosecutor soon. In an unrelated development, Azry Akmar said police had opened two investigation papers following a recent altercation at a religious school in Bukit Ibam, Rompin.

items.title: PKR’s Hassan Karim urges Anwar to retain Anthony Loke ahead of major transport projects
items.summary: PASIR GUDANG, Sept 22 — Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim has called on Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to persuade Anthony Loke to remain as transport minister to ensure the completion of several key infrastructure projects, including those in Johor. The PKR lawmaker expressed concern that Loke’s resignation could jeopardise ongoing projects, including those in Johor. “I hope the prime minister takes my view into consideration and persuades Loke to stay.

items.title: Malaysia’s research has potential, now it needs to leave the lab, says higher education minister
items.summary: Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said the milestone demonstrated Malaysia’s immense capacity for innovation, provided the gap between academic research and commercial market demands could be bridged effectively. “Malaysia had many good researchers, ideas and promising innovations, but too many of them remained at the university level. “For the first time, we are creating a dedicated platform for university researchers to bring their ideas directly to industry, investors and potential partners,” he said during the opening ceremony of the University Research and Innovation Investment Summit 2026 at the Kuala Lumpur Convention Centre here today.

items.title: No drug arrests for a week? Kelantan police chief says two station heads get reprimand letters
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 22 — Two police station chiefs (OCSs) in Kelantan have received reprimand letters after they failed to record any drug-related arrests for a week, said state police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat. He said the state police headquarters is monitoring seven police stations with regard to enforcement against drug abuse and trafficking. Mohd Yusoff said the performance of each police station is monitored weekly and presented at meetings with the head of the Narcotics Department.

items.title: Finance pros cannot escape geopolitics in a changing world, says deputy finance minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Finance professionals must adapt to a rapidly changing global landscape shaped by geopolitical shifts, climate and sustainability challenges, artificial intelligence (AI) and growing concerns over trust. Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong said the transformation of the global environment in recent years had created new challenges for businesses and finance professionals, requiring them to rethink how financial systems and structures are designed. As such, he emphasised the need for financial professionals to understand geopolitical developments worldwide, particularly as businesses face growing risks to investment, technology and supply chains.

items.title: Melaka heads for polls as CM Rauf Yusoh confirms assembly set for dissolution tomorrow
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 22 — The Melaka State Legislative Assembly will be dissolved tomorrow to pave the way for the 16th state election. Ab Rauf said State Assembly Speaker Datuk Ibrahim Durum had also submitted the notice of dissolution to the Election Commission (EC). They were former Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Idris Haron (BN-Sungai Udang), Datuk Nor Azman Hassan (BN-Pantai Kundor), Datuk Noor Effandi Ahmad (Bersatu-Telok Mas) and independent Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee (Pengkalan Batu).

items.title: Three actors out on bail as police hunt uploader of viral Rukun Negara clip from 2018
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Bukit Aman have released three local actors on police bail after questioning them over a viral video of a 2018 theatre performance allegedly mocking the Rukun Negara, while investigators hunt for the person who re-uploaded the footage. “The three have since been released on police bail after their statements were recorded, and checks found no content from the performance on their mobile phones or other devices. The performing arts centre has since closed, Kumar said.

items.title: Zahid: Neither MB Ismail Lasim nor I was summoned by Negeri Sembilan Ruler for an audience
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 22 — Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said neither he nor Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim was summoned for an audience with Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir at Istana Negeri Sembilan here yesterday. Neither the Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar nor I was ever summoned for an audience. The institutions and establishment in Negeri Sembilan must also be respected,” he said.

items.title: Melaka heads for polls? CM Ab Rauf set to make big announcement today
items.summary: MELAKA, Sept 22 — Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh is expected to announce the dissolution of the Melaka State Legislative Assembly at 2pm today, paving the way for the 16th state election. Speculation over an imminent dissolution intensified after the state executive council meeting, usually held on Wednesdays, was brought forward by a day. In the 2021 Melaka state election, Barisan Nasional (BN) won 21 of the 28 seats contested, while Pakatan Harapan (PH) secured five and Perikatan Nasional (PN) two.
